title: Is Tomac Bikes About to Make a Comeback?
content:
John Tomac is one of the most legendary mountain bikers the sport has ever known. In a racing career spanning from the mid 1980’s to the early 2000s, “Johnny T” was renowned as one of the most well-rounded cycling athletes of his time. From professional road racing to top results in both XC and DH, John Tomac excelled at racing virtually anything with two wheels. Ultimately, he tried to leverage his notoriety and experience into a mountain bike brand.

In the late 1990s, Tomac partnered with Manitou’s founder Doug Bradbury and founded Tomac Bikes. In 1998, the brand debuted with three full-suspension models. After a few years, the name was licensed to American Bicycle Group and ultimately acquired by Joel Smith, who operated Tomac Bikes from 2006 to 2013. 

Now, 13 years later, a Tomac Bikes account on Instagram just appeared out of nowhere and is teasing what appears to be a comeback for the brand. The first post (above) is from October 29th, and says “THE LEGEND RETURNS. A new chapter begins.” The second post (below) is from yesterday, November 19th, and it includes a link to the Tomac Bikes website, which is simply a landing page where you can enter your email address to get on the mailing list. Whether John Tomac or his son, motocross superstar Eli Tomac, is involved remains to be seen.

So, whether you’re feeling nostalgic for the old days when John Tomac dominated nearly every cycling discipline, or you just want to know what Tomac Bikes is cooking up, you can click on the link below to sign up. We can’t wait to find out, and we’ll keep you posted when we know more.
